### What the decision must establish

| Decision question | Required answer | Evidence and present boundary |
|---|---|---|
| What is being proposed? | Classify a dispatched worker supervising native helpers separately from an agent-launched handoff owner, person-opened peers and command-internal Agent helpers. Do not treat all four as one `--sub` mode. | R01 role matrix; R03 §§2–4; R05 launcher inventory. Ordinary launches do not automatically create Run/Task/Dispatch records or a worker preamble on the inspected paths. |
| What additional value is sought? | Identify coherent, independently checkable work discovered during execution, and the material upper-coordinator round trip that local supervision would avoid. Distinguish that benefit from parallelism already available under one coordinator. | R06 trigger evidence; W02 external guidance: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents and https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system . No qualifying local measured saving was established. |
| Is the capability technically available? | Credit current native local helper machinery: same-Run Task/Dispatch ancestry, creator-directed reports/questions, reply validation, fencing and selected-mail handback. Keep successful live operation separate. | R03 §§1–3 provides installed-source tracing. It supersedes older root-only mailbox predictions and earlier slice-local statements that routing was entirely unknown. |
| Is its use authorized? | State the approved policy before describing any exception: WC-13 prohibits worker-session fan-out at any depth; section 4 admits a person-opened coordinator. Resolve the ownership-rule conflict explicitly. | CONTRACT §§1, 3–4; CORE launch guidance; R01/R06; defect A01 below and INF-027. Native support is not authorization. |
| What must be changed conceptually? | Decide session eligibility, bounded planning/launch/retry authority, command-versus-session placement, exclusive Task ownership and the treatment of a proposed role flag. | R01 full rule-by-option matrix; R06 D1–D5; R07 current change surfaces. This is a decision about responsibilities, not a sequence of implementation tasks. |
| What does completion mean? | Separate child completion, the middle session's own completion, aggregate outcome, artifact validation and result admission. Preserve blocked/failed/partial inputs and original child evidence. | R02 signal/state tables; R01 section-4 matrix; W02. Existing flat admission is present; recursive composition is the missing definition. |
| Who remains responsible after failure? | Name the owner of children, pending questions, mixed deliveries, intervention budgets, freezes and cleanup when the middle session asks upstream, is fenced, exits, exhausts context or is replaced. | R02 §§2–3 and Gaps; R03 handback trace; W02 external supervision analogy: https://www.erlang.org/doc/system/sup_princ.html . Handback is not complete monitoring transfer. |
| What does security require? | Separate inbound delivery, authenticated origin, permitted requests, authorization before effects, human consent, replay/revocation state and safe destructive-action predicates. | W01/W03. A delivered message or valid credential is not a human Ruling, permission to fan out, or proof a worktree may be deleted. |
| Which scopes remain independent? | Keep #339 supervision, #423 knowledge sharing and hierarchy/delegated authority separate; preserve #409 as observation rather than control. | R08 requirements and issue comparisons. Shared release wording does not establish shared acceptance criteria. |

### Behavior a subordinate capability would have to provide if adopted

| Area | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Identity and scope | Bind the subordinate to a trusted parent, explicit role, permitted resources and a bounded assignment. The role name, worktree ancestry and absence of a worker preamble must not manufacture authority. |
| Downward delegation | Permit only the approved creation/start routes and explicitly bounded helper count, depth, retry and write scope. Preserve exclusive ownership of self-created Tasks or deliberately replace that rule. |
| Upward reporting | For native local helpers, use the established creator-Dispatch route rather than assume a missing transport. For an ordinary handoff owner, define correlation, progress, questions, acknowledgments, completion and failure reporting without impersonating worker lifecycle messages. |
| Supervision | Distinguish the middle session's progress from child activity; service parent instructions and children without discarding mixed batches; keep delivery acknowledgment separate from application acknowledgment. |
| Results | Admit actual child contracts and artifacts before declaring aggregate success or starting dependents. A launch receipt, heartbeat, idle notice or child status message must not substitute for admitted completion. |
| Recovery and budgets | Preserve lineage limits, applied-message history, outstanding deliveries, uncertain side effects and ownership across replacement. Parent settlement must not be treated as proof that descendants are stopped. |
| Human authority | Carry eligible clarification answers with their provenance, but keep Rulings, permission prompts, frozen-plan handback and outward publication with their authorized human-facing owner. |
| Cleanup | Require current settlement, admission, writer quiescence and protected-state checks. Neither a close request nor a valid grant proves that cleanup preconditions hold. |
| Governed operation | Deliberately reconcile launch, reporting and required supervision probes with bound-session policy; do not rely on an executable-recognition ceiling as an authorized route. |

These are adoption conditions. The research establishes neither that all are implemented nor that the current policy has approved them.",

| SC03 — Rule-conflict disposition | The PR #449 ownership sentence versus WC-13/person-opened coordinator conflict is recorded as a severity-rated defect with INF-027 cited. | Fail if it is dismissed as documentation-only future work or treated as an approved worker exemption. A01. |
| SC04 — D1 interpretation | `--unattended` remains the explicit command-side unattended selector; the answer separately decides whether `--sub` changes role/topology and command eligibility. | Fail if all other flags are called forbidden, or hierarchy/environment detection silently replaces explicit mode selection. CONTRACT §1; R01 §2; R06 §5. |
| SC05 — Command boundary | The answer distinguishes CONTRACT's broad no-Orca-command sentence, WC-8's three named verbs and WC-13's six routes, and acknowledges the coordinator-only claim implementation tension. | Fail if omission of `agent launch` from WC-8 is used as a loophole or an Orca-calling orchestrator command is assumed automatically exempt. A04. |
| SC06 — Measured need | Reopening D5 is supported by a defined composite brief and a qualifying real-run record identifying the runtime-only split and material extra round-trip cost. | Adoption condition not established: a command chain is not a composite delegation brief, and the bounded notes search found no qualifying combined record. R06. |
| SC07 — Depth and version evidence | Source classifications, default/stored/effective settings, local versus remote behavior and public versus installed versions are separated. | Fail if current source tracing is called wholly missing, stored `1` proves the active value, a new Run resets depth, or public default `4` is substituted for installed default `1`. R03/W04. |
| SC08 — Aggregate admission | An adopted role defines own-versus-child progress, all outcome reductions and evidence-backed admission before completion/dependents. | Adoption condition unmet: flat admission exists, recursive result semantics do not. A08. |
| SC09 — Messaging and acknowledgments | An adopted role identifies one authoritative consumer/acknowledgment owner per stream, handles complete mixed batches and distinguishes receipt from application. | Adoption condition unmet; no nested live handling or measured cross-level response bound established. A09. |
| SC10 — Recovery | Every child remains assigned a supervisor through parent ask, fencing, exit, exhaustion and replacement, with persistent lineage budgets and freeze/cleanup responsibility. | Adoption condition unmet; selected-mail handback and public shutdown claims do not establish complete local takeover or subtree quiescence. A10/A20. |
| SC11 — Human and outward authority | No role, relayed message or token is accepted as a human Ruling, new Task-specific commit grant or permission to publish/merge/delete. | Fail if the middle worker inherits section-4 outward duties wholesale or a parent grant is assumed transferable. A11/A23/A27. |
| SC12 — Governed compatibility | The decision addresses trusted role binding, recognized launch/report operations, literal-executable coverage and the missing required supervision probes separately. | Adoption condition unmet. Person-opened does not prove unbound; `worker-show` does not make `worker-list`, `worker-read` or `worktree ps` available through the same branch. R04 B1/B2. |
| SC13 — Transport/security precision | The answer records the documented inbound hook, the partly unresolved sender-class mechanism, authenticated-origin and fail-closed gaps, and the limits of typed text and tokens. | Fail if it preserves an absolute no-inbound-hook claim, proposes all-bypass as necessary, or calls schema/signature validation complete authorization. W01/W03; A21–A24. |
| SC14 — Evidence fidelity | Every GQ gap/stale family is represented or explicitly deduplicated; current addenda and scope approval control older returns. | Fail if research-gate Minor is reused as implementation-impact severity, archival exclusions become runtime proof, or superseded W02 metrics are repeated. Coverage and correction tables below. |
| SC15 — Scope separation | #339 supervision, #423 knowledge sharing, hierarchy and observer-only #409 have distinct acceptance boundaries. | Fail if a v2 name, dashboard scale scenario or knowledge catalogue is counted as a working subordinate supervisor. A26/A29/A30. |
| SC16 — Read-only delivery | Sections 3 and 4 contain complete decision content but no implementation sequence, runtime trial or authorization/settings change. | This synthesis was returned inline; persistence and checklist bookkeeping remain parent-owned. No source/runtime changes or tests were performed. |",
    "{{RF_PLACEHOLDER:constraints}}": "| Constraint | Binding interpretation |
|---|---|
| D1 — Explicit mode | CONTRACT §1 and SPEC D1 require explicit unattended selection and prohibit command detection of Orca, its preamble or environment. D1 is not a ban on output/depth/other ordinary flags. A `--sub` flag that grants supervision would change authority/topology and needs its own explicit disposition. |
| D2 — Person-only Rulings | CONTRACT WC-3 and freeze/resume rules retain actual human acceptance. A parent agent's reply is not a Ruling; a coordinator cannot draft one or retry around a frozen plan. |
| D3 — PR carriage | PR submission remains an ordinary top-level session for the named PR, never a dispatched worker. A subordinate label does not change that rule. |
| D4 — Narrow local grant | A worker's permitted local commit requires the person's exact Task-specific instruction, sole occupancy of its Orca child worktree and a succeeded command result. It ends at that Task's completion; no transitive child grant or outward authority follows. |
| D5 — Reconsideration gate | SPEC D5 retains depth 1, person-opened coordination and WC-13. Both a defined composite brief and qualifying measured runtime-only split are required to revisit. Historical AC-0.7 completion is distinct from current tracing; R03 now supplies current source classifications. REC additionally names establishing the depth-2 mailbox, omitted from SPEC's short row; that discrepancy must remain visible. |
| Command versus session | CONTRACT's opening sentence says commands contain no Orca calls. WC-8 names three fan-out verbs; WC-13 separately covers six routes from the worker session at any depth. Moving a call out of a command does not evade WC-13. Existing coordinator-only claim code is a boundary tension, not a blanket worker exemption. |
| Orca depth ceiling | R03 traces worker-start and dispatch, including inject/dry-run, through depth checks. Task creation and ordinary worktree/agent launches are not depth-checked, but task creation has independent coordinator-authority checks. A new Run does not reset caller delegation depth. General launches create no supervised identity automatically on the inspected paths. |
| Scope of setting | Installed default and inspected stored value are 1; active loaded value and safe lowering remain unverified. The inspected setting is runtime/profile-wide, not a demonstrated per-Run switch or a proven machine-wide/all-profile setting. Public migration/default changes do not alter this investigation's local policy. |
| Hook ceilings | The worktree hook is a bounded agent-flag syntax check; the launch guard uses positively bound session identity and literal `orca` recognition; job identity is Linux same-user process selection, not a sandbox. Do not transfer one hook's declared ceilings to another. Missing role fields cannot be supplied by naming a session. |
| Governed-session restrictions | Recognized non-exempt Orca operations and SendMessage receive ESCAPE, denied at every governed level. The literal matcher does not establish all-executable coverage. Required enumeration/transcript/prompt-wait probes are separately missing from the recognized exceptions. No alternate spelling, allowlist expansion or bypass is authorized. |
| Lifecycle and evidence | Preserve top-level worker lifecycle ownership, exact attempt identity, full-batch processing, actual report reading, admission before dependents, bounded retries and non-destructive handling of silence. Internal helpers do not become independent Orca lifecycle owners. |
| Worktrees, Git and cleanup | Preserve distinct writers, setup authorization, one outward/integration owner, protected worktrees, unread reports, unfinished ledgers, frozen plans and task evidence. Worktree ancestry is placement/identity information, not supervisory authority. |
| Distribution | R07 distinguishes canonical source, plugin mirrors, generated development copies, installed copies and packaged artifacts. Sync/build/install are not one automatic operation; installers may preserve old copies. Source-visible rules and tests do not certify universal installed freshness. |
| Research scope | This investigation is read-only: no live Orca run, worker launch, mailbox consumption, acknowledgment, setting change, permission change, model change, API write, implementation or source mutation. Unverified runtime questions remain limitations rather than authorized experiments. |
| Evidence precedence | Installed-source R03 mechanics govern older guesses and slice-local unknowns. R04/R05/R07 B1/B2 addenda govern immutable original returns. R07's approved current-source inventory scope governs older partial-status wording; unread archives remain excluded background. W02's controlling metric correction governs its original JSON. External context supplements, never overrides local source and policy. |",

Important means a material policy, integration, operational or value question must be decided before relying on it. Minor means bounded historical, citation, administrative or background uncertainty. These are not claims that a live exploit or data-loss incident occurred. GQ's existing research-gate Minor dispositions remain unchanged; explicitly documenting a risk was enough for that research gate, not for safe implementation.

### Current defects and adoption gaps

| Gap | Current State | Target State | Severity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A01 — DEFECT: subordinate-role rule conflict | CORE and the installed ownership wording name a coordinator under another orchestrator, while WC-13 prohibits worker fan-out and section 4 admits a person-opened coordinator. A launched nonworker is not expressly promoted to coordinator by CONTRACT's user-started ordinary-session clause. | A coherent role definition or an explicit narrowing of ownership wording, with a recorded decision about supervised and nonworker cases. | Important | GQ G02/G51; R01/R06/R08. This is an in-scope contradictory/unwired rule defect, not merely future work. **INF-027 at INF:78** expressly deferred changing WC-13 to a separate sub-orchestrator/coordinator issue; INF-026 at INF:77 excluded supervised workers from that ownership change. That scope decision explains the unresolved defect; it does not close it or authorize an exception. |
| A02 — No approved subordinate delegation contract | Existing command chains do not define discretionary child planning, launch scope, helper/question counts or an autonomous composite brief. Current D1–D4/WC-13 policy is established package-wide, despite slice-local unknowns. | Explicit eligibility, scope and bounds for any adopted role; deliberate WC-13/D5 amendment if a dispatched worker may supervise. | Critical | GQ G03/G33; R01 full matrix/R06. Otherwise the capability would perform prohibited operations under an undefined grant. Policy decision needed, not a live test to discover current rules. |
| A03 — D1 and proposed `--sub` authority switch | Explicit unattended selection exists; hierarchy-aware command behavior or a second authority selector is not defined. Other ordinary flags are not prohibited by D1. | A clear distinction between unattended command behavior and subordinate session authority, including any flag's exact meaning and eligibility. | Important | GQ G35; R01 §2/R06 §5. No implicit environment/preamble detection and no inference that adding a flag grants authority. |
| A04 — Orca-calling command boundary unresolved | The broad no-Orca-command rule, WC-8's three verbs and WC-13's six routes coexist with actual coordinator-only claim helper calls. A proposed orchestrator command has no established exception. | An explicit coordinator-command boundary or session-only design decision; preserve WC-8 unless deliberately changed. | Important | GQ G35; R01/R05/R08; stale family S31. This affects even a root-only orchestrator, not only sub mode. The shorter WC-8 list is not a launch loophole. |
| A05 — D5 need trigger not established | No qualifying record combining a runtime-only split, Task identity and material measured extra round-trip cost was found in the bounded search. Long runtimes, follow-ups and public requests do not satisfy it. | Decision evidence satisfying the actual two-part trigger, or an explicit approved replacement decision. | Important | GQ G10; R06 trigger table; W02/W04. No global claim that such notes cannot exist elsewhere. No measured speedup or supported worker capacity follows from external examples. |
| A06 — D5 mailbox prerequisite divergence | REC requires establishing the depth-2 question/completion mailbox before a raise; SPEC's short approved row omits it. Intentional waiver versus summarization loss is unknown. | A recorded interpretation of the discrepancy, distinguishing source-established routing from live validation requirements. | Important | GQ G11; R06 §2. R03 answers the local source destination; that does not resolve the historical omission's intent or certify live recovery. |
| A07 — Residual upward protocol for ordinary owners | Native local helpers have a source-established upward route. Ordinary agent/worktree launches do not automatically create a supervised parent link or worker records, and no complete ordinary-owner reporting lifecycle was established. | Define trusted parent/correlation, progress, questions, acknowledgments, completion, failure and admission for a nonworker owner, without lifecycle impersonation. | Important | GQ G19/G51; R03 §§2–4/R02 §4/R05. This replaces the overbroad claim that every form lacks an upward channel. A new protocol is needed for this role; a new transport or message type is not proved necessary. |
| A08 — Recursive progress, outcome and admission | Flat result admission/fan-in exists. Own-versus-child progress, aggregate failed/blocked/partial reduction and subtree completion are undefined. Complete backend report-file validation was not traced. | Aggregate results retain each required child's status and evidence; contracts/artifacts are read and admitted before dependent work or aggregate success. | Important | GQ G04/G24; R01/R02; W02. A launch receipt, status, heartbeat or idle notice cannot substitute for admission. A correct child result is not automatically a correct aggregate. |
| A09 — Mixed mailbox scheduling and acknowledgment | Parent instructions and helper reports can share the middle Dispatch FIFO. Source provides Delivery replay/generation fencing, but application scheduling and whole-batch ownership remain unverified. | One authoritative consumer handles all relevant messages before batch acknowledgment; separate delivery receipt from applied/queued/refused acknowledgments at each edge. | Important | GQ G05; R02/R03/W01. Live behavior remains untested. Receiving an upstream answer does not prove a child applied it; wake filters are not separate semantic queues. |
| A10 — Subtree recovery, retry, freeze and cleanup ownership | Selected reports/questions can return to the Run after creator settlement, but that is not full supervision takeover and selected unread handback excludes heartbeat. Parent ask/fence/exit/exhaustion/replacement can leave child duties unresolved. | Explicit child owner, settlement ordering, orphan handling, persistent lineage budgets, cancellation authority, freeze propagation and cleanup responsibility through every parent transition. | Critical | GQ G06/G07; R02 states/ladder, R03 handback. G06 has live scope; G07 first needs policy. Public newer helper stopping is not installed proof and retains preserved-descendant/uncertain-stop/remote exceptions: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38373 . Parent stopped is not subtree quiescent. |
| A11 — Human escalation and non-transferable authority | L5 means report to the person. Rulings, permission prompts, PR carriage, frozen-plan handback and Task-specific commit grants retain their present boundaries. No transitive grant is established. | Preserve actual human provenance, one authorized outward owner, relay acknowledgment/deadlines and Task-specific authorization without agent-generated acceptance. | Critical | GQ G08/G34; R01/R02/R06; W01 external boundary: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging#how-a-session-treats-an-incoming-message . Signing or forwarding an agent message cannot turn it into consent. |
| A12 — Trusted role signal absent from hook bindings | The worktree hook checks syntax; the launch guard records launch levels and consumes session/tool fields, not parent/role/depth/resource/action scope. Job identity is not orchestration authorization. | Any adopted exception is based on trusted, scoped authority rather than role names, prompt assertions or arbitrary record words. | Important | GQ G27; R04 identity table; W03. This is not a claim that all hooks see only command text. A new launch-record word currently does not create a valid role. |
| A13 — Governed launch and upward-message policy | In positively bound sessions, recognized non-exempt Orca forms receive ESCAPE; SendMessage is independently ESCAPE. Every governed level denies that class. | Deliberately decide whether and how scoped launching/reporting belongs in governed sessions, including child-policy binding and permitted destinations. | Important | GQ G52; R04 B1/B2/R05/R07 addenda. Satisfying the agent flag does not satisfy the launch guard; no blanket exception or permission escalation follows. |
| A14 — Literal-executable enforcement ceiling | The Orca branch recognizes basename `orca`; research observed `orca-ide`, which does not match that branch. Other classifications can still deny an invocation. | State and assess actual coverage before claiming reliable enforcement; do not mistake a mismatch for authorized operation or proven bypass. | Important | GQ G52; R04 B1. Static defect/ceiling remains even though overbroad research wording was corrected. No alternate-spelling experiment or live success is claimed. |
| A15 — Required supervision probes conflict with governed classifier | Recognized `worker-list`, `worker-read` and `worktree ps` are absent from the exceptions, despite required enumeration, transcript and prompt-wait duties. `worker-show` is listed but not equivalent. | A coherent policy for the complete supervision duty, separate from launch and message permissions. | Important | GQ G52; R04 B2; CONTRACT supervision versus GUARD exceptions. A bound O1/O2 supervisor also faces this issue; person-opened does not establish unbound status. No automatic allowlist expansion is recommended. |
| A16 — Depth fence is not complete authority enforcement | Current source settles the call classification: worker-start/dispatch are depth-fenced; task-create and ordinary agent/worktree launches are not. Task creation independently requires coordinator authority. General launches do not create Dispatch identity automatically. | Keep per-call depth, role permission and runtime evidence distinct; bound any adopted launch authority beyond depth alone. | Important | GQ G17; R03 §§1/6. This is not the older 'three routes guarded only by prose' claim: independent task-create authority must be retained. Actual refusal receipts/session identity remain live-unverified. Depth is not total-worker, spending or isolation control. |
| A17 — Active setting, rollback and version migration | Installed default/stored profile are 1; loaded effective value, external-edit reload and safe lowering remain unknown. Same-runtime/profile scope is source-backed; a public per-Run override was not found, not universally disproved. | A decision grounded in the actual host/build/effective scope and reversible lifecycle behavior, without substituting public defaults or all-machine assumptions. | Important | GQ G14–G16; R03 §5/W04. Live setting/reversal questions remain. External v1.4.251 default-4 migration can also change an older intentional unmarked 1; its effect on this installation is untested: https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/38348 . |
| A18 — Local lifecycle, federation and build-equivalence evidence | Installed source establishes native local routing, reply/fence/handback paths.
